rooms.title: The Parcel Depot

sources.label: Nell’s old parcel
sources.hint: Talk to Nell and accept the parcel once. It holds ten beats in eight different note kinds.

sources.label: The small delivery chest
sources.hint: Nell points out a small chest beside her counter. Its half note is needed for every opening door.

doors.label: The garden door
doors.hint: Two quiet beats, then two sounding beats.

doors.label: The workshop door
doors.hint: A long step, two quick steps, then four tiny steps.

doors.label: The canal door
doors.hint: A long step, one ordinary step, then paired footsteps.

rooms.description: Mira finds three doors and three people with different reasons to seek the silent bell.

rooms.title: Iris’s Garden Porch

sources.label: Iris’s listening phrase
sources.hint: Iris gives back the two kinds used at the garden door. These are needed for the next garden gate.

doors.label: The overgrown arch
doors.warning: A faded answer is scratched beside the arch. Iris warns that the path behind it is overgrown.

rooms.description: Iris asks Mira to listen to the space between notes. Her gift is claimed once through conversation.

sources.label: Pip’s running phrase
sources.hint: Pip offers a half note, paired eighths, and four sixteenths. The workshop gate needs that precise phrase.

doors.label: The silent aviary
doors.warning: The birds turn away from this door. Pip says its long call has nowhere to return from.

sources.label: The stamped delivery chest
sources.hint: The ferry keeper points out a chest bearing Nell’s postage. Its three notes match the lock ahead.

doors.label: The empty ferry
doors.warning: A rotted boarding rope hangs beyond this door. The ferry keeper warns that no boat waits there.

doors.label: The hearth path
doors.hint: A three-beat call followed by an ordinary step leads toward the homes.

doors.label: The old stone path
doors.hint: The small groups, a breath, and two different half-beat replies lead deeper into the old garden.

doors.label: The schoolroom stair
doors.hint: A three-beat call and one ordinary step lead toward the shared music room.

doors.label: The birds’ back passage
doors.hint: Two quiet beats, another quiet beat, then two different half-beat replies lead behind the birds’ stage.

doors.label: The town-bell stair
doors.hint: A three-beat call followed by four tiny steps climbs toward the public bell.

doors.label: The copied waterway
doors.warning: The ferryman’s map shows that this quiet passage ends at a wall.

doors.label: The home door
doors.hint: Use the five note tiles you carried here: two kinds of groups, a quarter rest, a single eighth, and paired sixteenths.

doors.label: The music-room door
doors.hint: Two quiet beats, one quiet beat, then the two different half-beat replies finish the phrase.

doors.label: The town door
doors.hint: Two quiet beats, one quiet beat, then two different half-beat replies complete the tower’s answer.

rooms.title: The Overgrown Music Box

sources.label: Four notes beneath the loose stone
sources.hint: Iris remembers a music box under a stone carved with a flower. Search there; the newly found phrase reveals the hidden gate.

doors.label: The hidden flower gate
doors.hint: The four newly found one-beat tiles open this gate.

rooms.description: The hidden pickup is inside the chosen secret branch. It cannot be collected on the normal path and cannot leak into a regular ending.

rooms.title: The Birds’ Dusty Attic

sources.label: Two long notes inside the hollow perch
sources.hint: Pip notices a perch whose two sides answer differently: one sounds and one stays silent. Search it to reveal the hidden gate.

doors.label: The hidden brass gate
doors.hint: A sounding half note and a silent half rest open the brass gate.

rooms.description: Searching is optional before choosing this detour. Inside it, the once-only hidden cache is needed for the only forward gate; it remains available until found.

doors.label: The unfinished-song door
doors.hint: The original three-beat call and the ordinary one-beat note were kept for this last answer.

doors.label: The birds’ answer door
doors.hint: Finish with the original three-beat call and the ordinary one-beat note you carried through the back passage.

terminals.title: The Overgrown Arch
terminals.repair: Revisit Iris’s porch and use her gift at the listening gate.

terminals.title: The Silent Aviary
terminals.repair: Revisit Pip’s workshop and use his running phrase at the workshop gate.

terminals.title: The Empty Ferry
terminals.repair: Revisit the canal storehouse, open the stamped chest, and use its delivery phrase.

terminals.title: The Copied Waterway
terminals.repair: Revisit the water clock and choose the town-bell stair.

rules: Doors accept their authored ordered recipe, not every rhythm of equal duration. Every door costs exactly four beats.
All sources are explicit interactions, claimed once globally per run. Talking again never gives another parcel. No notes are awarded automatically on room entry.

Nell supplies eight kinds worth ten beats; the depot chest holds the missing half note worth two beats. Both opening interactions are naturally required: every door needs the half note, and that note alone is not four beats. Garden and workshop notes come from conversations; canal notes come from a chest.
The source required for a good porch gate gives exactly the kinds absent after the corresponding opening door. The gate therefore cannot be paid before claiming it.
Hidden sources exist only after choosing their secret detour. Their fixed four-beat gate spends exactly the newly supplied four-beat vector before the branch rejoins its own final room.
Successful terminal stock must equal zero for every kind. Dead ends retain four or eight beats. Nothing discards, converts, or consumes arbitrary leftover notes.
Undo restores room, inventory, source receipts, revealed doors, and the committed action log together. Permanent discoveries never provide current-run notes.
The previous automatic three-tile-per-stage grants are replaced by these explicit once-only sources.

budgetProof.regular: 12 initial beats + 4 branch-source beats = 4 doors × 4 beats = 16; zero remains.
budgetProof.secret: 12 initial beats + 4 branch-source beats + 4 hidden-cache beats = 5 doors × 4 beats = 20; zero remains.
budgetProof.typed: Each branch’s remaining eight beats are partitioned into two fixed four-beat vectors. The regular path spends A then B; the secret path spends B, its newly supplied cache vector, then A. Equality holds component by component.
